frozen_original.title: USDA/RFK Dietary Guidelines Politicized; NIH Nutrition Research Gutted
frozen_original.synopsis: In March 2025, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and RFK Jr. announced a 'line-by-line review' of the 2025 Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee's science report, with Kennedy pledging guidelines as short as four pages — compared to the prior 164-page document — potentially contradicting scientific consensus on saturated fats, seed oils, and red meat. The NIH's lead ultra-processed food researcher resigned in April 2025 after 21 years, citing fear of censorship. The Trump budget proposed cutting NIH nutrition research funding while also eliminating the CDC's National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion ($1.4 billion annual budget). Scientists and CSPI condemned the MAHA Commission's strategy report for including fake citations and pseudoscientific claims, while the administration canceled over $1 billion in local food funding and terminated NIH grants covering nutrition and diet-related disease research.

frozen_original.title: DOJ Investigates January 6 Committee Members for 'Prosecutorial Misconduct'
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, the DOJ launched investigations into members of the House January 6 Select Committee — including Representatives Adam Kinzinger and Adam Schiff — for alleged 'prosecutorial misconduct' in handling witness testimony and evidence related to the Capitol attack investigation. The investigations were universally described by legal experts as legally baseless and retaliatory, as congressional committee members conducting oversight have broad constitutional immunity for their legislative activities. The episode was seen as part of a systematic effort to criminalize legitimate congressional oversight and deter future investigations into executive branch misconduct by threatening political retaliation against investigators.

frozen_original.title: DOGE Proposes Eliminating Social Security Disability Benefits
frozen_original.synopsis: In March 2025, documents and public statements from Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency revealed proposals to eliminate or dramatically restructure Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) — the program that provides income support to over 8 million Americans with severe disabilities who cannot work. DOGE officials characterized SSDI recipients as lazy or fraudulent despite SSA data showing denial rates of over 60% and average annual benefits of approximately $16,000. The proposals included dramatically tightening medical eligibility criteria, shortening benefit periods, and converting SSDI from an earned benefit to a capped block grant. Disability rights organizations warned that implementing the proposals would force millions of severely ill and disabled Americans into destitution. The proposals provoked significant bipartisan congressional opposition.
